questions.stem:
At time $t$ seconds, $t>0$, a particle $P$ is at the point with position vector $\mathbf{r}$ m, where
$\mathbf{r} = (t^4-8t^2)\mathbf{i}+(6t^2-2t^{\frac{3}{2}})\mathbf{j}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the velocity of $P$ when $P$ is moving in a direction parallel to the vector $\mathbf{j}$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme: Accept column vectors throughout this question. M1: Differentiate $\mathbf{r}$ (both components) — In each component at least one power going down by 1. A1: $\mathbf{v}=(4t^3-16t)\mathbf{i}+(12t-3\sqrt{t})\mathbf{j}$ (Accept as two separate components). DM1: Equate $\mathbf{i}$ component of $\mathbf{v}$ to zero and solve for $t$ — Dependent on the first M1. Must start with a component of the vector for $\mathbf{v}$. Can have more than one value at this stage. A1: Obtain $(24-3\sqrt{2})\mathbf{j}\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$ (Accept $20\mathbf{j}\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$ or better. (19.757359...) Correct answer only. Answer must be a vector)

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme: M1: Differentiate $\mathbf{v}$ (both components), even if the method for obtaining it was incorrect — Their $\mathbf{v}$ must be a vector. In each component at least one power going down by 1. A1: Obtain $\mathbf{a}=(12t^2-16)\mathbf{i}+(12-\frac{3}{2}t^{-\frac{1}{2}})\mathbf{j}$ (Any equivalent form for acceleration). A1: Obtain $176\mathbf{i}+\frac{45}{4}\mathbf{j}\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$ (Accept $180\mathbf{i}+11\mathbf{j}\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$ or better. ISW)

questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are unit vectors, with $\mathbf{i}$ horizontal and $\mathbf{j}$ vertical.]
Figure 3 shows the fixed points $A$ and $B$ which lie on horizontal ground.
At time $t = 0$, a particle $P$ is projected from $A$ with velocity $(4\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
Particle $P$ moves freely under gravity and hits the ground at $B$, as shown in Figure 3.
At time $T_1$ seconds, $P$ is at its highest point above the ground.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme: M1: Complete method using suvat $4-gT_1=0$ or $T_1=\frac{\sqrt{32}\sin 45^\circ}{g}$. A1: $T_1=0.408\,(0.41)$ (3 sf or 2 sf only. Not $\frac{20}{49}$)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
At time $t = 0$, a particle $Q$ is also projected from $A$ but with velocity $(5\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
Particle $Q$ moves freely under gravity.
(b) Find the vertical distance between $Q$ and $P$ at time $T_1$ seconds, giving your answer to 2 significant figures.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme: Height of $Q$ above $P$: M1: Complete method using suvat and 7 and 4 for the initial vertical components. A1: $h=(7T_1-\frac{1}{2}gT_1^2)-(4T_1-\frac{1}{2}gT_1^2)$ $(=3T_1)$ Correct unsimplified expression in $T_1$ or their $T_1$. They do not need to have substituted for $T_1$ (2.0408...–0.8163...). A1ft: $h=1.2\,(\mathrm{m})$ (2 sf only $(3\times$ their $T_1)$)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
At the instant when particle $P$ reaches $B$, particle $Q$ is moving at $\alpha^\circ$ below the horizontal.
(c) Find the value of $\alpha$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme: B1: Correct time for $P$ to reach $B$. ($\frac{40}{49}$, 0.816, or $\frac{8}{g}$ or better) Seen or implied. M1: Vertical component of speed $=7-g\times 2T_1$ $(=-1)$ Complete method using suvat with $2T_1$ or their $t$ for the time at $B$. M0 if not using 7. M1: $\tan\alpha=\pm\frac{\text{their }1}{5}$ Correct use of their 1 and 5 to find an equation in a relevant angle (e.g. $90-\alpha$). A1: $\alpha=11$ (11 or better (e.g. 11.3)). Note: If they use $T_1$ in place of $2T_1$ can score B0M0M1A0

parts.label: d
parts.text:
At time $T_2$ seconds, the direction of motion of $Q$ is perpendicular to the initial direction of motion of $Q$.
(d) Find the value of $T_2$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme: M1: Form an equation in $T_2$ only. Complete method using suvat and perpendicular gradients. e.g. $\begin{pmatrix}5\\7\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}5\\7-gT_2\end{pmatrix}=0$ Condone sign errors (Vertical component of speed $=\pm\frac{25}{7}$) (perpendicular direction is downwards at 35.5° to the horizontal). A1: $-\frac{25}{7}=7-gT_2$ Correct unsimplified equation. A1: $T_2=1.08$ or $T_2=1.1$ (3 sf or 2 sf only)

questions.stem:
Figure 4 shows a uniform rod $AB$ of length $8a$ and weight $W$.
The end $A$ of the rod is freely hinged to a fixed point on a vertical wall.
A particle of weight $\frac{1}{4}W$ is attached to the rod at $B$.
A light inelastic string of length $5a$ has one end attached to the rod at the point $C$, where $AC = 5a$.
The other end of the string is attached to the wall at the point $D$, where $D$ is above $A$ and $AD = 5a$, as shown in Figure 4.
The rod rests in equilibrium.
The tension in the string is $T$.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme: M1: Moments about $A$: Need all terms and no extras. Dimensionally consistent. Condone sign errors and sine/cosine confusion. M0 if there is no resolving. A1: $4a\cos30^\circ\times W+8a\cos30^\circ\times\frac{W}{4}=5a\cos30^\circ\times T$ Correct unsimplified equation. A1*: $6W=5T\Rightarrow T=\frac{6}{5}W$ Obtain given answer from correct working, e.g. show cancelling of the common factors or some simplification of the moments equation

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find, in terms of $W$, the magnitude of the force exerted on the rod by the hinge at $A$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme: They need 2 equations. Award M1A1 for the first correct equation seen and M1A1 for the second correct equation. Common alternatives: M(B): $T\cos30^\circ\times3a+V\cos30^\circ\times8a=W\cos30^\circ\times4a+H\cos60^\circ\times8a$; M(C): $W\cos30^\circ\times a+H\cos60^\circ\times5a=\frac{1}{4}W\cos30^\circ\times3a+V\cos30^\circ\times5a$; Perpendicular to rod: $\frac{1}{4}W\cos30^\circ+W\cos30^\circ+H\cos60^\circ=T\cos30^\circ+V\cos30^\circ$; Parallel to rod: $\frac{1}{4}W\cos60^\circ+T\cos60^\circ+W\cos60^\circ=V\cos60^\circ+H\cos30^\circ$. M1: First equation dimensionally correct. Condone sine/cosine confusion and sign errors e.g. Resolve horizontally. A1: $H=T\cos30^\circ$ $(H=\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{5}W)$ Correct unsimplified equation. M1: Second equation dimensionally correct. Condone sine/cosine confusion and sign errors e.g. resolve vertically. A1: $V+T\cos60^\circ=W+\frac{W}{4}$ $(V=\frac{13}{20}W)$ Correct unsimplified equation. DM1: $|R|=\sqrt{V^2+H^2}$ or $|R|^2=V^2+H^2$ Correct use of Pythagoras. Dependent on two preceding M marks. A1: $|R|=\frac{W}{20}\sqrt{3\times144+169}=\frac{\sqrt{601}}{20}W$ 1.2W or better (1.22576...)
